conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. The displacement model uses real V = H¹₀(D; Rᵈ), gradient norm, Q = L²₀(D), and b(v,q) = −∫q div v on nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domains in dimensions two and three. The Dirichlet condition covers the full boundary.
The measurable shear modulus satisfies 0 < μ₀ ≤ μ ≤ μ₁ almost everywhere; λ is a nonnegative scalar. Strain is the symmetric gradient and stress is 2με(u) + λ(div u)I.
For finite λ > 0, p = −λ div u and the second mixed equation is b(u,q) − λ⁻¹(p,q) = 0. At λ = ∞ use λ⁻¹ = 0; at λ = 0 use the primal problem with p = 0.

The discrete pair is exactly continuous P1 displacement enriched by vector cell bubbles, with zero boundary values, and continuous mean-zero P1 pressure. Meshes are conforming shape-regular affine simplicial meshes exactly fitting a polygonal or polyhedral domain.
The algebraic gauge requires symmetric positive-semidefinite K, a full-column-rank R spanning the entire kernel, and compatible load Rᵀf = 0; it returns the representative with Rᵀu = 0.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice and the stated real elasticity and mixed conventions, the continuous problem has a unique solution for every λ ∈ [0,∞], using the primal problem and p = 0 at zero and the incompressibility constraint at infinity. On polygonal/polyhedral domains with a conforming affine simplicial mesh family having a common shape-regularity bound, the mini problem is uniquely solvable. The continuous solution bound and displacement-pressure best-approximation error bound have constants depending only on d, D, μ₀, μ₁ and the common shape-regularity bound, independently of λ and h.

Assume Countable Choice and the displacement-model data. For every finite λ ≥ 0 there is a unique u ∈ V satisfying Eλ(u,v) = f(v). Its V norm is at most μ₀⁻¹‖f‖, its energy norm is at most μ₀⁻¹ᐟ²‖f‖, and every finite-dimensional conforming Galerkin space has a unique solution with V-error bounded by ((2μ₁ + dλ)/μ₀) times the best V-approximation error.

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded open D, finite λ > 0, and u ∈ H¹₀(D; Rᵈ), p = −λ div u belongs to the well-defined mean-zero subspace of L²(D). On the stated nonempty connected Lipschitz model domains in dimensions two and three, this is exactly the imported pressure space Q.
Under the gauge algorithm's K and R hypotheses, the augmented matrix [K R; Rᵀ 0] is nonsingular. For compatible f, its solution has multiplier zero and is the unique u satisfying Ku = f and Rᵀu = 0.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly inherited countable-choice assumption for Sobolev completion, closure approximation, and variational solvability.
Weak derivatives, Sobolev classes, and the H¹ norm controlling gradients.
H¹₀ as the H¹ closure of compactly supported smooth tests and passage of integration identities to zero-boundary fields.
Hilbert completeness of H¹ and its closed zero-boundary subspace under Countable Choice.
Real L² Hilbert structure and completeness of the closed mean-zero pressure subspace.
Continuity of strain, divergence, load and pressure pairings.
Integrability and boundedness of the integral functional on L² over bounded domains.
Representative independence of the mean-zero pressure condition.
Linearity of the mean-zero pressure subspace and scalar multiplication of zero-mean divergence.
Unique continuous displacement solvability for the bounded coercive real elasticity form.
Unique finite-dimensional conforming Galerkin solvability and the explicit M/α displacement error estimate.

concerns.concern: Steps 5.1–6.1 use the block form Aλ without explicitly defining it, and step 6.1 invokes “β ≥ min(Cdiv(D)⁻¹, β*) > 0” although β* is never introduced. The intended block form follows from the mixed equations and the intended uniform discrete lower bound is supplied by F5; these are recoverable notation omissions.

seams_checked.note: Checked the imported spaces, zero-mean divergence, Dirichlet Korn/Poincaré identities, continuous inf-sup, Babuška–Brezzi theorem, exact mini spaces and Fortin stability against their actual statements. Domain, sign, Countable Choice and common shape-regularity assumptions are retained.

The contact-model definition imports only the algebraic strain and elasticity-form conventions. It explicitly distinguishes its partial-trace displacement space and supplies local coercivity and well-posedness rather than applying the full-boundary Dirichlet theorem.

The declared page prerequisite is contextual. The current ALE page and its listed item carriers contain no elasticity-supplier citation; their diffusion-transmission and moving-grid claims do not import elasticity solvability or incompressible stability.

The isogeometric elasticity theorem reproduces the finite-λ displacement theorem's domain, coefficients, real gradient-norm space, Countable Choice and finite-dimensional conformity hypotheses, including the exact (2μ₁ + dλ)/μ₀ factor. It explicitly disclaims a λ-uniform or locking-free NURBS conclusion.
